title: Sunset Clock
prayerNote: Counted from sunset, which is 00:00. Local clock time on the right.
summaryText: Many traditions begin the day at sunset rather than at midnight. Sunset Clock shows how long it has been since the last sunset, a count that restarts the moment a new day begins, or how long remains until the next one. The sky behind it follows the real position of the sun.
techText: Sun positions are calculated on your device with the NOAA solar equations, so it works offline and your location is never sent anywhere. Sunrise and sunset use the sun’s centre 0.833° below the horizon to account for refraction and the size of the sun’s disc. Prayer times are calculated estimates and may differ by a minute or two from official tables; check with your local authority. The Hijri date uses the Umm al-Qura calendar, moved forward at sunset, and may differ by a day from local moon sighting.
notesText: In his books (Resāle-ye Novin, Emām-shenāsi vol. 6, Matla‘-e Anvār vol. 10), Allameh Sayyid Muhammad-Husayn Husayni Tehrani (1345–1416 AH) proposes “sunset-set” clocks: each day at sunset, set the hands to 12. In his view the night precedes the day, so the reckoning starts at sunset, and one glance shows how much night has passed and how much day remains. He argues that the common noon-set clock, anchored to midnight and noon, lacks this benefit, calling it the “European clock” and the sunset-set one the “Sharia clock”. Per Wikipedia, before Iran’s official time was unified in 1935, clocks were apparently set by noon or sunset. This app shows the same idea digitally and automatically: 00:00 is your location’s real sunset. Sources: maktabevahy.org, nooremojarrad.com.
liveOn: Live notification is on (best effort, see “Notification limits”). Press pause on the notification to stop it.
liveFail: Couldn’t start the live notification on this device or browser.
installText: Install: in Chrome on Android tap the ⬇ button (or ⋮ → Install app). On iPhone use Share → Add to Home Screen. Live notification: tap 🔔 to show the running clock in your notification shade and on the lock screen. It is a media-style notification kept alive by a silent audio track, so it has a pause button that turns it off, and your phone may stop it to save battery. Web apps have no other way to show a ticking clock.
creator: Creator
gpsFail: Couldn’t get your location. You can type coordinates instead.
gpsOk: Location found. Press save to use it.
badCoords: Enter a latitude from −90 to 90 and a longitude from −180 to 180.
polar: The sun doesn’t cross the horizon here today, so sunset is approximated.
limitsText: The live notification is a workaround, not a true notification. It plays a silent audio track so your phone shows a media player, and that only works while your browser or the installed app keeps running. Your phone may stop it at any time (battery saver, closing the app, and on some devices locking the screen), and then the clock freezes. It shows text only, and the system may update it less often than once a second. It can take over the media controls from music or podcast apps. iPhone support is limited and it may not appear at all. This app cannot send prayer reminders or alarms while it is closed: web apps need a push server for that, and this one has none. For reminders, use your phone’s alarm or a dedicated prayer-times app.
